oidc_jwt.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows and bearer-token usage documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same unexpired access token as replay unless a one-time artifact is being tested.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes are one-time and short-lived by design.
oidc_jwt.note: A second successful exchange would be suspicious; a failed second exchange is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: The nbf claim is optional and lack of nbf enforcement is spec-compliant.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance of tokens without nbf, or future-nbf handling alone, as a vulnerability without stronger product-specific evidence.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token rotation may be enabled or intentionally suppressed by client policy.
oidc_jwt.note: Reuse or non-rotation behavior can be policy-driven and is not automatically a replay vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of JWTs without nbf, or platform behavior that does not enforce nbf, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing nbf enforcement alone as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Brokered OIDC public keys obtained from JWKS URL are cached for performance, so old keys may remain accepted until refresh.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance of old signatures before cache refresh as a trust-anchor violation.

oidc_jwt.description: When an administrator changes issuer, JWKS URL, or validating key for an external OIDC identity provider, acceptance under the new trust anchor is expected.
oidc_jwt.note: This is an authorized configuration change, not attacker-controlled trust substitution.

oidc_jwt.description: The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing client_id in aud is by design unless an audience mapper explicitly adds it.

oidc_jwt.description: Federated usernames may be lower-cased unless case-sensitive username is enabled on the identity provider.
oidc_jwt.note: Lowercasing of brokered usernames is expected normalization, not necessarily an identity collision.

oidc_jwt.description: First broker login flows may create a new user, link to an existing account, or auto-link depending on configured authenticators.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges caused by configured broker linking flows are by design and must be separated from unintended principal collapse.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes are one-time, short-lived temporary codes and cannot be used more than once.
oidc_jwt.note: Second use failure is expected and should be asserted via status/error, not treated as instability.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 authorization-code replay tests, the authorization code issued by /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth is documented as one-time and short-lived. A valid replay test must reuse the SAME code at /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token and assert the second exchange fails; do not treat failure as a setup bug.

For PKCE tests, client setting 'PKCE method' blank means PKCE is optional, not disabled. To test pkce_skip or pkce_not_required_public_client correctly, first create a control client with PKCE method explicitly set to S256 or plain; otherwise omission of code_verifier is by configuration and not a vulnerability.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching, with wildcard support only at the end of the URL pattern. For redirect_uri_mismatch and related I3 tests, do not assume glob semantics beyond documented suffix wildcards; mismatches in case or path should be treated as distinct URIs.

For I5 audience tests, Keycloak documentation states the frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token aud claim. Do not expect access tokens to contain client_id as audience unless an Audience or Audience Resolve mapper adds it; otherwise empty or missing audience for the frontend client can be by design.

For I5 audience_mismatch and cross-provider_jwt_audience style tests, audiences in access tokens are driven by client scopes, role scope mappings, and audience protocol mappers. The fuzzer MUST configure audience-producing mappers/scopes first; otherwise a missing aud claim may reflect configuration, not failed enforcement.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation and token_exchange_wrong_audience tests, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor 'downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer' that restricts exchanged scopes to those already present in the subject_token/assertion. The fuzzer MUST record whether this executor is configured; rejection of expanded scope is expected when enabled.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests, a client scope with role scope mappings only applies if there is an intersection between the user's roles and the client scope roles. If no intersection exists, the scope and its mappers are omitted from the token. Do not misclassify missing claims as stripping bugs without verifying client-scope permission prerequisites.

For I4 case-confusion tests on brokered identities, the identity-provider setting 'Case-sensitive username' controls whether the federated username is preserved or lower-cased. If disabled, username lowercasing is by design for federated identities; compare against normalized values or enable case-sensitive mode before asserting collisions.

For I4 account-linking and cross-user-collision tests, the default first broker login flow intentionally prevents automatic linking of an existing local account solely by matching email/username because this is documented as a potential security hole. Tests must distinguish explicit linking flows from automatic import behavior.

For I4 multi-identity tests involving organization group mapping, Advanced Claim to Group supports exact matching by default and regex matching only when 'Regex Claim Values' is enabled. Do not use wildcard or regex patterns unless that flag is enabled; otherwise values are exact-match only.

For I1 issuer-validation tests against brokered OIDC identity providers, the IdP configuration field 'Issuer' is the value Keycloak validates against responses from the external IDP. If Issuer is unset or misconfigured in the test setup, issuer-validation conclusions are invalid.

For I1 signature-validation and key-rotation tests against brokered OIDC identity providers, 'Validate Signatures' must be ON. If it is OFF, Keycloak will not verify external ID Token signatures, so alg_none, resign_attacker_key, kid_injection, and trust-anchor tests are not meaningful.

For I3 signing-key rotation tests against brokered OIDC identity providers using JWKS, Keycloak caches the external provider public key for performance. Acceptance of old signatures before JWKS cache refresh is not sufficient evidence of stale trust; only acceptance after cache refresh/expiry should be treated as a failure.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control login using a valid token/session in the same realm/client configuration. A failed attack login at the token endpoint or broker callback is otherwise indistinguishable from broken client configuration, missing scopes, or invalid redirect URI setup.

Client secret rotation uses numeric sentinels with exact meanings: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'use default'. Do not assume 0 disables rotation; it forces immediate invalidation of the previous secret.

Password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses sentinel -1 to mean 'use algorithm default iterations' rather than literal negative or disabled. Do not treat -1 as disabling hashing-iteration checks; it selects the documented default for the chosen algorithm.
Password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses sentinel 0 to mean the user must always re-authenticate before password update, not 'no limit'. Do not interpret 0 as disabled.

WebAuthn/WebAuthn Passwordless policy 'Timeout' uses sentinel 0 to delegate timeout behavior to the authenticator implementation, not a literal zero-second timeout and not disabled validation. Tests must not assume deterministic timeout semantics when set to 0.
User session count limiter uses sentinel 0 to disable the session-limit check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Do not interpret 0 as zero allowed sessions.

Authentication session sub-session limit authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 per root authentication session, and when the limit is reached the oldest authentication sub-session is removed. Multi-tab or repeated auth-start tests must account for eviction rather than assuming all pending auth sessions remain valid.

PKCE method has sentinel semantics: blank means PKCE is not required, though clients may still send PKCE parameters; S256 or plain means that exact challenge method is required. Do not assume blank disables PKCE support; it disables enforcement only.

For I3 PKCE tests, if the client's PKCE method is blank, exchange without code_verifier may succeed by design. To test PKCE enforcement, configure the client with PKCE method S256 or plain before running the sequence.

Authorization codes are one-time, short-lived temporary codes and cannot be used more than once. Reuse failures at the token endpoint are expected and should be asserted via non-200 status, not identity comparison.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default. Wildcards are only supported at the end of the URL pattern, and wildcard comparison is disabled when the passed redirect URI contains userinfo or parent-directory path traversal '/../'. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, use exact registered values unless explicitly testing the documented trailing-wildcard behavior.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the redirect_uri supplied to the token request must match the authorization request and a registered valid redirect URI. A mismatch rejection is expected behavior, not a bug.

When testing OIDC request object signature handling, the client policy layer may enforce Request Object Signing Algorithm. If no such policy is configured, acceptance or rejection of unsigned request objects may reflect client policy configuration rather than a protocol bug. Establish a control with the same client configuration.

For I2 expired_token and future_token style tests against issued tokens, include a control login using a valid token flow in the same realm/client configuration. Otherwise, token endpoint or userinfo failures may be caused by client misconfiguration, missing scopes, or disabled grant types rather than freshness enforcement.

The organization scope has exact request semantics with three documented forms only: 'organization', 'organization:<alias>', and 'organization:*'. For multi-organization tests, do not invent wildcard patterns other than the literal documented 'organization:*'.

Client scopes permissions are intersection-based: if a client scope has role scope mappings, the user must have at least one intersecting role or the scope is not applied and will not appear in the token scope. For I5 scope-escalation tests, ensure the subject user is actually permitted to use the requested optional scope; otherwise missing claims are expected.

Role scope mappings limit roles in issued access tokens. By default, new clients effectively get all user role mappings unless Full Scope Allowed is turned off or scope mappings are narrowed. For I5 least-privilege tests, explicitly configure role scope mappings; otherwise broad role inclusion is by default configuration.

Audience in access tokens is not automatically the frontend client itself. Audience is typically added through Audience Resolve or hardcoded audience mappers. For I5 audience tests, configure audience-producing mappers or client-role-based audience resolution first; otherwise missing aud for a target service is expected.

For token exchange downscoping tests, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor that restricts exchanged scopes to those already present in the initial subject_token. Without that executor, broader scopes may be granted according to normal client configuration. Do not interpret broader exchanged scope as a vulnerability unless the downscope policy is configured.

For token exchange audience tests, use the audience parameter only with the token exchange grant. The documentation states audience simulation is currently only supported for token exchange. Do not expect audience parameter effects on other grants.

Refresh token rotation has sentinel semantics at the realm/client-policy level: with Revoke Refresh Token enabled, a refresh token becomes invalid after use; with suppress-refresh-token-rotation client policy, subsequent refresh responses may omit new refresh tokens and rotation is intentionally skipped. Distinguish these modes before asserting replay behavior.

Client secret rotation has sentinel semantics: Rotated Secret Expiration = 0 means the old secret is removed immediately during rotation, not 'inherit default'. Secret rotation does not happen automatically in the background; it occurs on client update or explicit regenerate action.

For OIDC SSO broker tests where Keycloak consumes external ID tokens, configure the external OIDC identity provider with Issuer and enable Validate Signatures with either JWKS URL or Validating Public Key. Without these settings, issuer/signature validation coverage is incomplete and I1 trust-anchor tests are invalid.

JWKS-based external OIDC IdP validation uses cached public keys for performance. After upstream key rotation, old keys may remain accepted until cache refresh. Only flag acceptance of old signatures after the documented cache refresh window/refresh event, not immediately after rotation.

The external OIDC IdP setting 'Allows client assertions to be re-used' changes replay behavior for federated client authentication. If enabled, repeated use of the same client assertion is by configuration and must not be flagged as an I2 violation.

The external OIDC IdP setting 'Allows Client ID as audience for assertions' is non-standard and, if enabled, treats the configured client ID as the only valid audience for assertions instead of token-url/issuer-url. Audience-validation tests for federated client assertions must account for this override.

Case-sensitive username handling for brokered identities is configurable. If 'Case-sensitive username' is disabled, the federated username is lower-cased and may not match the original upstream value. For I4 case-confusion tests, record whether this setting is enabled before treating case folding as identity collapse.

First broker login can automatically link or create users depending on the configured First Login Flow. Auto-linking existing accounts is explicitly documented as dangerous but supported. For I4 principal-binding tests, distinguish by-design account linking flows from unintended identity collapse.

The general identity provider setting 'Essential claim value' supports regular expression format, while 'Essential claim' name matching is case-sensitive. For multi-identity tests, do not assume wildcard semantics on claim names; only the value field is documented as regex-capable.

The token endpoint supports multiple client authentication methods: Authorization Basic, form client_id/client_secret, signed JWT, federated signed JWT, and X509 depending on client configuration. A failed token request may reflect client-auth method restrictions rather than grant rejection. Use the configured allowed authentication method in controls and attacks.

Mutual TLS certificate-bound access tokens and refresh tokens are sender-constrained. UserInfo and refresh requests with such tokens require successful client certificate verification, and these tokens cannot be used as subject_token in standard token exchange. Do not treat such rejections as generic token invalidity.

PKCE method blank means PKCE is optional, not disabled as a protocol feature. If blank, clients may still send PKCE parameters, but Keycloak will not require them. For I3 PKCE enforcement tests, configure the client with PKCE method=S256 or plain; otherwise a missing code_verifier may be accepted by design.

Authorization codes are one-time and short-lived. The same code cannot be used more than once. For I3 code replay or code injection tests, assert rejection on second use or cross-session reuse via HTTP status, not identity comparison.

The token endpoint returns both identity and access tokens in some flows, but session_token for subsequent API calls MUST be access_token, not id_token. UserInfo and other bearer-protected endpoints require the access token.

Refresh token rotation is configurable. When 'Revoke Refresh token' is enabled, a refresh token becomes invalid after use and the client must store the newest refresh token from the latest response. When refresh token rotation is suppressed by client policy, subsequent refresh responses may not return a new refresh token. Do not assume one behavior without checking client policy and realm settings.

For I2 replay_same_token on ordinary bearer JWT access tokens, reuse is by design unless the token is a one-time artifact such as an authorization code or a rotated refresh token. Do not flag repeated use of a valid access token as a vulnerability.

OIDC broker issuer validation depends on the configured Identity Provider 'Issuer' field. Keycloak validates issuer claims from the external IDP against this configured value. For I1 trust_anchor_substitution and issuer-validation tests against brokered OIDC login, the IdP configuration MUST include Issuer; otherwise issuer comparison may not be meaningfully constrained by the tested setup.

OIDC broker signature validation depends on 'Validate Signatures'. If this switch is OFF, Keycloak will not verify signatures on external ID Tokens. For I1 alg_none, resign_attacker_key, kid_injection, and trust_anchor_substitution tests against brokered OIDC login, Validate Signatures MUST be ON and a trust source configured via JWKS URL or validating public key.

When brokered OIDC uses JWKS URL, Keycloak caches the external provider public keys for performance. After key rotation, old keys may remain accepted until cache refresh. For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests against brokered OIDC, only flag acceptance of the old key after the JWKS cache should have refreshed; immediate continued acceptance can be due to documented caching.

When brokered OIDC uses a static validating public key and 'Validating Public Key Id' is unset, that key is used for all requests regardless of the key ID sent by the external IDP. For kid-based tests, do not expect kid mismatches alone to fail unless a specific Validating Public Key Id is configured.

The broker can enforce an essential claim from the external ID token. 'Essential claim' name matching is case-sensitive and 'Essential claim value' supports regular expression format. For I5 claim-binding tests on brokered OIDC, exact claim-name casing matters, and regex semantics apply only to the value field, not the claim name.

Create User If Unique checks for existing accounts with the same email or username and may create or link accounts depending on the first broker login flow. This can collapse distinct upstream identities into one local account by configuration. For I4 collision tests, distinguish by-design account linking flows from unintended identity collapse.

Organization and broker group mapping can assign users to groups based on external claims. The 'Advanced Claim to Group' mapper supports exact matching by default and regex matching only when 'Regex Claim Values' is enabled. For I4/I5 multi-identity tests, do not use wildcard-like values unless regex mode is explicitly enabled; otherwise values are exact matches.

Client scopes affect both claims and audience. Optional client scopes are applied only when requested via the scope parameter; default client scopes are always applied. For I5 empty_audience and scope-escalation tests, ensure the requested scope set matches the intended token contents, otherwise missing or extra claims/audiences may be due to client-scope configuration rather than a vulnerability.

Client scope permissions are intersection-based: if a client scope has role scope mappings, the user must have at least one intersecting role or the scope is not applied and will not appear in the token scope. For I5 tests involving optional scopes or audience mappers, ensure the test user actually has the required roles; otherwise the scope silently disappears by design.

Access token roles are the intersection of roles assigned to the user and the role scope mappings the client is permitted to access. For I5 authorization-binding tests, expected permissions must be computed as user roles ∩ client role scope mappings, not all user roles.

The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. Audience is added through audience resolve or hardcoded audience mappers. For I5 audience tests, do not assume the client_id will appear in aud unless a mapper or token-exchange audience parameter causes it.

For token exchange and JWT assertion grants, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor that restricts requested scopes to those already present in the initial subject_token or assertion JWT. If this downscope executor is enabled, only downscoping is allowed and any extra requested scope must be rejected. I5 scope-escalation tests must check whether this executor is active before interpreting results.

The token introspection endpoint requires client authentication and can use HTTP Basic or other supported client authentication methods. For introspection-based verification, authenticate as the client rather than using the bearer access token being introspected.

Default ACR Values are not a reliable enforcement mechanism. A client can still request a lower acr_values value unless Minimum ACR Value is configured. For I5 or step-up tests, use Minimum ACR Value to enforce a floor; do not rely on Default ACR Values alone.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. Multi-tab browser logins may restart automatically, and expired authentication sessions can cause protocol-specific errors that clients may retry. For I3 state/session coherence tests, distinguish expired authentication-session behavior from cross-session confusion.

User session count limiter uses numeric sentinel 0 to disable the check for both maximum realm sessions and maximum client sessions. Value 0 does not mean zero sessions allowed; it means no limit. Never interpret 0 as a strict denial setting.

The authenticationSessions SPI authSessionsLimit uses a numeric limit on authentication sub-sessions per root authentication session. Default is 300, and when the limit is reached the oldest authentication sub-session is removed after a new authentication request. This is eviction, not denial. Tests involving many parallel browser auth attempts must account for oldest-session eviction.

For I2 expired_token and future_token style tests on OIDC tokens, include a control login using a valid token or valid flow parameters. A failed attack login alone cannot distinguish token freshness enforcement from broken client configuration, redirect URI mismatch, or missing client capability.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
